Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real roots. Use the quadratic formula (x = [-b ± √(Δ)] / 2a) to find the roots. If Δ = 0, there's one real root (x = -b / 2a). To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function (f'(x)). Set the first derivative equal to zero (f'(x) = 0) and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine the nature of the stationary points, find the second derivative (f''(x)) and evaluate it at the x-coordinates of the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
